The Project aims at external promotion of Ukrainian MSMEs, establishing inter-regional and international partnerships, in particular with representatives of the business community of the Republic of Croatia, learning best business practices from experienced Croatian entrepreneurs, increasing marketability and digital presence of Ukrainian MSMEs. The proposed Project will be integrated into the comprehensive UN Recovery and Peacebuilding Programme (UN RPP), which addresses priority needs in eastern and southern Ukraine following the outbreak of the armed conflict in the spring of 2014.

title: EE - IUU fishing combating
description: Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated fishing poses a threat to sustainable fisheries and aquatic biodiversity, exacerbated by weak governance, risks of corruption, and impacting livelihoods, food security, and multiple Sustainable Development Goals. The project seeks to combat IUU fishing in Ukraine by deploying innovative technologies (drone surveillance, GPS tracking) and increasing the capacity of responsible actors, including State Agency of Melioration and Fisheries of Ukraine, raising public awareness.

title: Digital, Inclusive, Accessible: Support to Digitalisation of Public Services in Ukraine (DIA Support) Phase 2
description: The Digital, Inclusive, Accessible: Support to Digitalisation of Public Services in Ukraine (DIA Support) Phase 2 Project is built on achievements and lessons learnt from the previous phase (2021-2023), and aims to continue to support the ongoing digitalisation process in Ukraine with the view of strengthening the Government’s capacities to deliver high quality and accessible digital services to vulnerable groups in Ukraine while using digital technologies and solutions to address other complex challenges posed by the war, including ensuring transparency and accountability of the recovery process, critically important for Ukraine’s EU Integration.

title: Ukraine Joint Programme on conflict-related sexual violence (JP_CRSV)
description: Four PUNOs, namely the O-SRSG-SVC, UNDP, UN Women and UNFPA will take part in the Joint Programme aiming to push the implementation of the Framework of Cooperation forward by responding to the immediate needs that the Inter-Ministerial Working Group is experiencing in terms of human resources. The joint project is anchored in providing technical support for the Implementation Plan, collaborating with civil society organizations and first responders. In response to the situation and challenges indicated above, UNDP in Ukraine is committed to delivering capacity-building initiatives and filling critical gaps in terms of assistance to survivors as assessed by the WPA Unit.Primary goal of the project outcome will be to strengthen capacity of the national authorities for victim-centred and gender-sensitive response to CRSV and support to victims and survivors. As a result the rights and needs of CRSV survivors in Ukraine will be properly addressed.Output 1. ensure strengthened and coordinated CRSV prevention and response in Ukraine, that will be achieved through three main workstreams: (1) strengthening of coordination around service provision including by integrating a survivor-centred approach and ensuring that services are made available where they are most needed, (2) policy development, (3) capacity building and trainings.

title: Harnessing the potential of vulnerable groups for stabilization and recovery of eastern and southern regions of Ukraine

Project action will be based on the adoption of Early Recovery and Humanitarian-Development Peace NEXUS approaches, whereby development solutions are implemented in a humanitarian setting to address urgent needs and further capacitate community stakeholders in addressing these needs and strengthen their resilience to future crisis.

This is to be achieved through: 1) Strengthening capabilities of Ukraine’s entrepreneurs representing creative industries for digitalization and internationalization, cooperation with Czech businesses in particular: a capacity building programme focused on digitalization and internationalization for creative industries prioritizing cooperation with Czech businesses and including series of online workshops and webinars as well as dedicated knowledge products. 2) Enhancing connections and cooperation of Ukrainian companies and business support organizations with foreign counterparts, Czech in particular: matchmaking between Ukrainian and foreign MSMEs and business support organizations, Czech in particular, trade missions, experience exchange visits and other events to promote cooperation 3) Improving business enabling conditions and opportunities for public-private dialogue: digital tools to facilitate public-private dialogue with the solution enabling the draft regulations impact analysis.

title: Transformational Recovery for Human Security in Ukraine
description: The primary objective of the project is to contribute to bring transformational recovery from widespread death, destruction, displacement, and suffering caused by the war in Ukraine and to promote Human Security in Ukraine by undertaking concerted immediate actions against interconnected and multidimensional threats that Ukraine is currently facing. To maximise positive results for transformational recovery, the project interventions will focus on the following 6 priority thematic areas for the project outputs, based on the three principles of human security, namely, i) freedom from fear (threats to the safety of people); ii) freedom from want (threats to basic needs); and iii) freedom to live in dignity (access to services and opportunities) throughpromoting protection, empowerment, and solidarity.

title: Strengthening Capacities of the National Police of Ukraine on Reunification of Families in Ukraine
description: The project is designed to bolster the forensic capabilities of the National Police as part of the broader The Ukraine Family Reunification Initiative. With the ultimate goal of reuniting Ukrainian children with their families as a consequence of the war. The main activities are the following: the delivery of mobile forensic equipment to enable swift DNA sample gathering, an analysis of international best practices in creating and managing genomic information databases for an update to the national database SLID, and the enhancement of the knowledge and skills of National Police forensic experts in utilizing new equipment and approaches for DNA data collection.

title: NDCP LT-LEDS_Climate Change_Ukraine
description: This Project Initiation Plan is a part of the global UNDPs flagship initiative, the Climate Promise: From Pledge to Impact - Leveraging the Climate Promise to turn enhanced Nationally Determined Contributions (eNDC) into ambitious climate action. The project is aimed at supporting the climate goals of Ukraine, and is a pivotal element of UNDPs broader effort to assist the country in enhancing its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement, with a specific focus on inclusive and genderresponsive governance, as well as financing mechanisms to enable effective delivery and tracking of climate commitments across various sectors.Key to this initiative is the collaboration with the Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Environmental Protection and Natural Resources and other critical stakeholders (including NGO sector) to draft and enact legislation.

title: Support to Community Driven Mine Action in Ukraine
description: The project aims to support the office of the UN Resident Coordinator in establishing capacity to coordinate community driven Mine Action and the coordination of a one UN Mine Action approach, as well as to support accelerating the construction of a national mine action logistics base.

title: PIMS-9678 Umbrella Programme to Support NBSAP Update and the 7th National Reports_Ukraine
description: The project is a part of the global programme, aimed to support countries in revising and updating their National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) in order to align with the recently agreed upon Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and enable effective implementation of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Kunming Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework at the national level. In addition, the Programme supports countries in preparing and submitting their 7th National Report on the implementation of the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

title: Implementation of SDGs in Ukraine in the context of recovery from the war and towards the European integration
description: Since February 2022 Ukraine has been focusing on addressing the challenges caused by Russia’s full-scale invasion. The ongoing full-fledged war is keeping the needs of the people of Ukraine, their safety and security on top of the agenda, and simultaneously brings new priorities, developments, and aspects of the national policies of the country. Just before the war started, Ukraine had been making steady progress in achieving 15 of the 17 SDGs. However, projections made by UNDP suggest that up to 90 percent of the population of Ukraine could face poverty and vulnerability to poverty if the war continues. Furthermore, women have been disproportionally affected by the war, accounting for more than half of the Internally Displaced People and of those needing humanitarian assistance in 2024. UNDP has been supporting the Government of Ukraine (GoU) in implementing several reforms that catalyse Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) attainment, including those related to democratic (transparent and accountable) governance, sustainable environment and energy efficiency, and in the past two years also addressing the far-reaching consequences of the escalated war. Additionally, following the European Councils decision to open accession negotiations with Ukraine on 14 December 2023, the Ukrainian Government initiated an active phase of preparations for Ukraines accession to the European Union. This process has concurrently contributed to Ukraines progress towards the SDGs, demonstrating how the European integration efforts can complement and enhance national development strategies aimed at achieving a sustainable future. In this context, it is of tremendous importance not to lose all the progress Ukraine has achieved in sustainable development and ensuring the efforts towards achievement of the SDGs constitute the backbone of Ukraine’s recovery processes as well as strong basis for the European integration.

title: Strengthening accountability for conflict-related sexual violence crimes in Ukraine
description: Since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation on 24 February 2022, there has been evidence and reports of war crimes, crimes against humanity and other serious violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, including conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV). Cases of CRSV crimes have been documented against women, men, girls and boys, and it is expected that the number of documented cases will continue to grow as the armed conflict continues and more evidence, survivors’ accounts, reports, and allegations come to lightIn order to support coherent action in addressing the situation and challenges indicated above, in May 2022, the Special Representative of the Secretary-General on Sexual Violence in Conflict (SRSG-SVC) signed, on behalf of the United Nations, a Framework of Cooperation (FOC) on the Prevention and Response to CRSV with the Government of Ukraine. An Implementation Plan for the FOC was also adopted in 2022 and a revised version was launched in December 2023.As part of the effort to advance the FOC and its Implementation Plan, UNDP in Ukraine established a close partnership with the UN Team of Experts on the Rule of Law and Sexual Violence in Conflict (TOE) to strengthen, through joint and coordinated activities, national criminal accountability mechanisms for CRSV, including the domestic legal and policy framework as well as the capacity of the Ukrainian justice system to conduct effective, victim/survivor-centred, gender-sensitive, and trauma-informed investigations and criminal prosecutions of CRSV. The new project builds on the results and lessons learned from the initial phase, leveraging successful strategies and identifying areas for improvement to further enhance the effectiveness of the justice system in addressing CRSV and ensuring justice for survivors.

title: Crisis response for securing reliable energy access in Ukraine (FPI Energy)
description: The overall objective of the proposed project is to facilitate work by public authoritiesto ensure reliable access to electricity, heat, water supply and sanitation amid the ongoing attacks on the energy infrastructure. UNDP will build on its presence and broad partnerships on sub-national, national and international levels to ensure effective delivery and impact.The UNDP Green Energy Recovery Programme is an integrated approach to address Ukraine’s needs to accelerate efforts towards a more diverse energy mix the project herein has been designed to respond to, and align with, the specific objectives of the overarching EU Emergency Support Programme in favour of Ukraine, which will:1. Contribute to meeting the immediate needs of the Ukrainian population directly or indirectly affected by the armed conflict.2. Increase the country’s resilienceThe key objective of the UNDP-FPI Project “Crisis response for securing reliable energy access in Ukraine is to promote self-sufficiency and sustainability in energy provision, aiming for universal access for the people of Ukraine, emphasizing locally-led recovery efforts with optimal adaptation of green energy sources and technologies. Ensuring access to energy is critical to strengthen the resilience of the people and critical infrastructure of Ukraine during the war.

title: Strengthening MSME Business Membership Organizations in Ukraine: Phase III
description: The project aims to boost the resilience and competitiveness of Ukrainian MSMEs, supporting inclusive economic recovery and sustainable development. It will align and integrate the BMO sector for better MSME representation, strengthen BMO capacities for organizational and financial sustainability, and improve public-private dialogue to enhance MSME policies. The project is fully aligned with the Country Programme Document for Ukraine (2025-2029) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Results Framework for 2025 -2029.

title: Inclusive Recovery Support for Resilience and Human Security in Ukraine
description: This project aims to stimulate urgent recovery and strengthen resilience against the widespread death, destruction, displacement, and suffering caused by the war in Ukraine, for promoting Human Security in Ukraine. The project will undertake multi-sectoral and integrated immediate actions against interconnected and multidimensional threats that Ukraine is currently facing.The project will promote rapid recovery from the devastation of war by comprehensively implementing the urgently required interventions, which include: the restoration of basic infrastructure (electricity, water, public facilities, etc.), enhancement of a safe living environment through clearance of mines and explosive remnants of war (ERW) and debris management and recycling, promotion of economic recovery with support for agricultural industries and small and medium-sized enterprises and social reintegration of war victims and veterans, strengthening of capacity and functions related to the implementation of anti-corruption policies, expansion of legal services to war victims and socially vulnerable people, and strengthening of governance in the formulation and implementation of reconstruction plans by the Ukrainian at the national and local levels.

title: Strengthening Digital Governance for Enhancing the Efficiency and Accountability of the Central Government of Ukraine
description: The project`s aim is to improve governance efficiency through digital tools for coordination, policy development, and decision monitoring. The key components of the Project are the following: (a) development and deployment of a digital project management system for the Government of Ukraine, ensuring a more structured and transparent decision-making process; (b) implementation of Diia for Civil Servants services, streamlining administrative workflows and enhancing digital interactions among government institutions; and (c) capacity development building for civil servants, equipping them with the necessary digital skills to effectively use modernized systems and ensure long-term sustainability.

title: UNDP Ukraine Climate Promise II: Advancing Green Finance and Inclusive NDC Implementation
description: This Project Initiation Plan is part of UNDPs global Climate Promise initiative, aimed at assisting Ukraine in advancing its enhanced Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement. The project focuses on supporting Ukraine’s climate goals by fostering inclusive, gender-responsive governance, integrating green finance mechanisms, and developing strategies for the effective delivery and tracking of climate commitments. This effort is crucial in supporting Ukraine’s transition to a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy. The project, initiated in response to Ukraines request through the NDC Partnership, aims to strengthen policy frameworks, regulatory provisions, and institutional capacities to accelerate the implementation of Ukraine’s NDCs. The focus areas include renewable energy development, sustainable environmental practices, and the establishment of a low-carbon economy.

title: Mykolaiv Strategic Partnership
description: The overall objective of the proposed Project is to accelerate the process of reconstruction and recovery in Mykolaiv Oblast, as part of the Mykolaiv-Denmark partnership, with a view to normalising the situation for the current population, facilitating the reintegration of IDPs and refugee returnees, and addressing the specific needs of vulnerable groups to ensure that no-one is left behind.
